component.name: Irida
component.summary: Design a colour palette and apply it to COSMIC

description.p: Irida is a palette designer for the COSMIC desktop. Pick a palette, draft one from a wallpaper, or edit its thirteen roles by hand while the preview and the contrast ratios follow every change.

Apply it to the COSMIC desktop, COSMIC Terminal, btop, Neovim, fastfetch, lsd, zsh and cava in one step, and undo it in one step. Link a dark and a light palette as a pair, compare with saved versions, and export a complete rice repository. A panel applet applies any saved palette with one click.

Six new targets: WezTerm, lazygit, GTK, qt5ct, qt6ct and Discord (Vencord or Vesktop, packaged or Flatpak; only the clients that are installed get the theme). The exported rice's switch.sh runs every install script the rice carries. A target entry may be limited to a folder that exists, and detection may list several config folders or Flatpak ids.

Escape closes the open role column and leaves the wallpaper screen. Deleting a paired palette and undoing an apply say which palette they touched, and the Try it live tooltip names tmux and Starship. On the command line, an unknown palette, an unknown target id, a second draft with the same name and an empty list all say what to do next. A user target path may start with $HOME, a path that is not absolute is skipped with a warning, the kitty and Ghostty reload hints show below their minimum versions, and TOML errors fit on one line. The .deb no longer embeds the build machine's home folder.

Four new targets: tmux, zellij, yazi and Starship. Starship and tmux apply live. A target may write several blocks and key lines into one file, and review fixes to undo, live sessions and the install scripts.
The wallpaper behind the preview stays inside the preview instead of covering the role tiles and the colour editor.
The preview stays on screen while you edit: roles are tiles on the left, and a role opens in a column on the right instead of a separate tab.

New from wallpaper drafts a palette from an image, and the preview draws over it. A panel applet applies saved palettes from the COSMIC panel. The editor is split into a Palette workspace and a Preview workspace.
